sentences.text: A cross-party group of MPs and peers has identified human rights risks posed by artificial intelligence (AI), arguing existing laws are ill-equipped to address the technology's rapid growth.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: The Joint Committee on Human Rights (JCHR) published a report calling for a new bill on AI to "address the scale and seriousness" of such threats.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: "Nowhere in the world, including the UK, has a current legislative and regulatory approach to AI that is fit for purpose," said Labour MP and committee chair Alex Sobel.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Labour education minister Georgia Gould said AI was creating opportunities but that it was critical the government was "responding to those risks" posed by the technology.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: In a summary of its 100-page report, the JCHR argued AI has been responsible for numerous abuses of human rights, citing examples including the use of AI to create sexualised images of women and girls, and scanning people's faces without their consent.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: The JCHR has advocated for the creation of a "single, independent AI oversight body... on a statutory basis", saying the current legal framework is "fragmented and difficult to navigate", "leaving gaps in protection".
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: The report goes on to call for "more demanding obligations for higher risk AI systems and models" at all stages of the "AI lifecycle".
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: It continues: "Some uses of AI should be prohibited outright because they are incompatible with human rights.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: What is clear is that at present we are unprepared to deal with its consequences however potentially dire they may be." The JCHR's 12 members are drawn from both Houses of Parliament and they currently include MPs and peers from the Labour, Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Monday's report comes amid growing anxiety over the challenges posed by AI.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Jacob Coxon, an AI researcher who quit Anthropic, told the BBC this weekend that staff developing the systems were "genuinely frightened" for the future of humanity .
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: An Anthropic spokesperson told BBC News that it was building "models with some of the strongest safeguards in the industry".
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Labour's 2024 general election manifesto said it would "ensure the safe development and use of AI models by introducing binding regulation on the handful of companies developing the most powerful AI models".
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: The government used the King's Speech in July 2024 to commit to bringing forward "appropriate legislation", but no dedicated AI bill appeared in this year's King's Speech.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Asked what had happened to the law promised by Labour, Gould told BBC Breakfast that the government "has been regulating" - including action to tackle non-consensual sexualised deepfakes and a bill linked to cyber security.

sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: On Saturday, the head of Anthropic, Dario Amodei, proposed a plan calling for the regulation of AI.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: Amodei's plan included global regulation, industry-wide regulation and independent monitoring of AI models as they are developed.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: He also urged the pace of development to be slowed down and the bosses of two rival AI firms, Sam Altman of OpenAI and Elon Musk, said they agreed with him.
sentences.article_title: MPs and Lords call for new law to address AI threat to human rights

sentences.text: One human rights concern raised in recent years is that AI can display biases against particular groups if trained on large datasets scraped from the internet which can include racist, sexist and other undesirable material.

sentences.text: The UK needs a "culture shift" in how it does business, Andy Burnham has said ahead of a meeting between some of Britain's biggest bosses and the government.

sentences.text: The prime minister said those who take risks in business should be backed by government and local leaders should have the power to work with companies.
sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.text: Burnham had been due to attend the meeting, but cancelled his engagements for Monday and Tuesday following the death of his father.
sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.text: The Labour government has been criticised for increasing costs for firms, such as with the employer national insurance and minimum wage changes under Burnham's predecessor Sir Keir Starmer.
sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.text: The meeting comes as Chancellor John Healey prepares for his first Budget next month, with rising borrowing costs in recent weeks adding to the pressure on government finances.
sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.article_title: 'Culture shift' needed in how UK does business, PM urges

sentences.text: The rising cost of renting a home in the UK has accelerated after a three-year slowdown - with tenants told to expect more pain to come.
sentences.article_title: Rent rises set to speed up in gloomy forecast for tenants

sentences.text: Average rental costs for new tenancies were up 2.6% in July compared with a year earlier, according to property website Zoopla.
sentences.article_title: Rent rises set to speed up in gloomy forecast for tenants

sentences.text: That remains lower than the rate of rising prices in general, but the property portal has forecast annual rent rises among privately rented homes will hit 4% or 5% by the end of the year.

sentences.text: It said there were fewer homes available to rent and - with potential first-time buyers put off by higher mortgage rates - competition for rental places in some areas was more intense.
sentences.article_title: Rent rises set to speed up in gloomy forecast for tenants

sentences.text: "Our latest report shows how sensitive the rental market is to even modest changes in how many homes are available for rent," said Richard Donnell, executive director at Zoopla.

sentences.text: Separately, the rising cost of renting has calmed recently.

sentences.article_title: Rent rises set to speed up in gloomy forecast for tenants

sentences.text: The UK's economy grew faster than expected in July partly helped by businesses using artificial intelligence (AI).
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The economy expanded by 0.4%, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said, whereas analysts had predicted no growth.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Growth in July was helped by a strong performance from the services sector, and particularly computer programming.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Experts said the figure showed the UK economy was proving resilient in the face of shocks such as the war in Iran, but they expect growth to slow in the months ahead as high energy prices affect households.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: July's figure follows growth of 0.3% in June and zero growth in May.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: According to the ONS director of economic statistics, Liz McKeown, there was evidence that businesses involved with AI and related technologies helped to boost the sector, not just in July but in May and June as well.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The ONS said many of the IT businesses reporting the largest turnover "appear to be involved with AI", though it said it is difficult to quantify the exact impact of AI.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: McKeown also said some businesses had said that the warm weather and football world cup had affected activity in July, although she said the effects "differed across industries, benefitting some businesses while creating challenges for others".
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The ONS said that in the three months to July, which gives a better underlying picture, the economy grew by 0.4% compared with the previous three months.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Rob Arnold, co-founder of Ascendea, an AI firm which employs nine people, believes the UK hasn't seen the real economic growth potential from the technology yet.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: He says his company is able to develop apps for other businesses "100 times quicker at a 50th of the cost" because of AI, but that the UK government needs to do more to invest in the sector as there are currently better opportunities in the US.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: He knows a few small UK-based AI firms that have either moved to the US or are thinking of doing so due to a lack of UK government support.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Alongside grants and funding, he says the government also needs to invest in training companies on how to use AI as it can be dangerous if not understood properly.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "It's like playing with a weapon," he says.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Paul Dales, the chief UK economist at Capital Economics, said July's data showed "the resilience of the economy in the first half of the year continued into the second half".
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: However, he added that higher energy prices and borrowing costs would soon start to hit growth, especially if the rises seen this week are sustained.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The Iran war has led to a sharp jump in oil prices, which has fed through to higher energy and fuel prices - affecting households and businesses.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: This rise in energy costs has led to fears that inflation will remain high, and increase the chance that central banks will hike interest rates to keep price rises under control.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: The Bank of England is meeting next week to discuss interest rates.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Economists widely expect rates to be held, but some have predicted an increase before the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Chancellor John Healey said the economy, was "demonstrating a welcome resilience, despite serious global uncertainty".
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "Our growth although still fragile was the fastest in the G7 in the first half of the year," he added.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "But, the conflict in the Middle East does have impacts here at home - from the cost of the weekly family shop to the cost of government borrowing." Healey is to present his first Budget in October.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: He told BBC News this week that he wants people to confident about the economy , despite acknowledging the challenge of "historic high" borrowing costs.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Shadow chancellor Andrew Griffith said nobody in the government "should be high-fiving themselves" over the latest figures.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "Our construction and production sectors are shrinking, unemployment is up under Labour, and we've got the highest government borrowing rates in almost 30 years." What's happening to the UK economy and how does it affect you?
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Are interest rates on the way up again?
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: Yael Selfin, chief economist at KPMG, said while July's headline growth figure was strong, it "masks a weaker picture for households".
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "Consumer-facing services contracted in July, as retail and hospitality activity fell following earlier increases in activity in the summer," she said.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "The war in the Middle East continues to drive a lot of the economic data, but the UK is the most exposed to the fallout," he said.
sentences.article_title: AI boom helps drive surprise UK growth in July

sentences.text: "Calls for pro-growth measures will get louder as the Budget nears, but whether or not the government has the room to act remains to be seen." sentences.text: The new battery-electric TransPennine Express trains are set to enter service in 2034 Work to create the UK's first battery-electric trains for long-distance main line services is set to begin in 2028, the Department for Transport (DfT) has announced.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The 29 new Adessia Stream trains are expected to enter service in 2034 and will be built at Alstom's Litchurch Lane factory in Derby.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The government said the investment of almost £1bn would help support more than 350 jobs at Alstom and a further 6,000 jobs across the UK supply chain.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said the new trains would deliver "faster, more reliable journeys to the north and thousands of British jobs for the next generation".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The managing director UK at Alstom said the fleet would transform journeys across northern England He added: "I've lost count of the number of times someone has stopped me to tell me about the train that never came.

sentences.text: "And when that happens, it means missed shifts, missed appointments, and missed opportunities.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Today, that starts to change." The DfT said the trains would help deliver the TransPennine Route Upgrade's aim to boost capacity by 30%, with thousands of additional seats a day across the Pennines by the early to mid-2030s.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: They will run between key destinations across the north including Liverpool Lime Street and Scarborough, Manchester Airport and Saltburn, and Manchester Piccadilly and Hull.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The DfT added journey times would be cut by up to 10 minutes between Manchester and Leeds, and up to 14 minutes between Manchester and York.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: The trains will be bought by rolling stock company Rock Rail and leased to TransPennine Express, the government added.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Alstom, which boasts the largest rolling stock train manufacturing site outside of China, secured a £370m contract in 2024 to produce 10 new London Elizabeth line trains.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: This came less than three months after a redundancy consultation put 1,300 jobs at risk at its Litchurch Lane factory, which dates back to 1876.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Rob Whyte, managing director UK at Alstom, called the latest agreement a "landmark moment for Britain's railway".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: He said: "We're absolutely delighted.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It's fantastic news for Alstom as a company but also for the city of Derby and the East Midlands.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "It's a great opportunity for us to continue our legacy.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "Unite's Alstom members have worked tirelessly in campaigning to ensure Derby's proud history of train making continues well into the future," she added.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander spoke to the BBC at Alstom, next to one of the new Elizabeth line trains.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: She said: "It's fantastic news that a city like Derby, that's got such a proud railway heritage, is also going to be manufacturing that new fleet of trains for the north of England as well.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It's about building the railway that the country needs to support the economy, but it's also about making sure that, in our economic heartlands - places like Derby - we've got really high skilled jobs for the future.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: "This contract alone means 40 extra apprentices here.
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: It secures 350 jobs at this facility and will support over 5,000 jobs in the wider supply chain as well." In a statement, DfT said journeys on the new fleet would be "quieter, smoother and more reliable", while offering "improved accessibility, more luggage space and onboard wi-fi".
sentences.article_title: Alstom to build new battery-electric train fleet

sentences.text: Step-free boarding - the "elimination of gaps between the train and platform" - are also being promised as part of a commitment to accessibility, alongside three dedicated wheelchair spaces, two accessible toilets, family-friendly areas and cycle and buggy storage on each train.

sentences.text: Primark has said it plans to launch a home delivery service in Britain, four years after it made its first foray into e-commerce.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: The retailer did not say when it expects to launch the service, but it has bought a warehouse in Sheffield to enable it to ship products to homes.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: The company said there was "opportunity for profitable growth" through home deliveries, which could help boost trade after Primark reported subdued sales following the recent hot weather.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: Analysts said the decision to offer home delivery after years of resistance - including through the pandemic - indicated that Primark was facing major challenges from ultra-fast-fashion brands such as Shein.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: Primark did not sell goods online until 2022, when it launched a click-and-collect service which meant shoppers still had to travel to pick up their purchases.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: Associated British Foods (ABF), which owns Primark, said the fashion chain would "continue to grow click and collect and... will in the future offer home delivery in Great Britain".
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: ABF predicts Primark's UK sales will grow by about 1% in the fourth quarter of the year.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: But like-for-like sales - a key metric in the retail industry, which strips out the impact of store openings and closures - are expected to be "broadly flat" in the UK, and fall 3% across its global operations.
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: It said sales of autumn/winter clothing started later than normal due to the hot weather in the summer, but "trading was stronger when the weather cooled towards the end of the quarter".
sentences.article_title: Primark finally set to launch home deliveries

sentences.text: The fast-fashion chain is struggling to compete with brands such as Shein and Boohoo, as well as alternative platforms such as TikTok Shop and Vinted, and in July said it was lowering prices on hundreds of clothing items.

sentences.text: For some bosses, it's less about having the perfect CV and more about the way you think, the questions you ask and whether you're prepared to take a chance.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Six business founders and leaders share the qualities they notice most and the advice they would give to people trying to get ahead.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlotte Tilbury says one of the biggest things that has driven her career is refusing to let other people set limits on what she can do.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Nothing is impossible in life - it's only your own limitations you give yourself." The beauty mogul says there will always be naysayers, and there were plenty of people who told her she was "mad" or that her ideas would not work but it's important to ignore them.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Tilbury recommends trying not to think of setbacks as mistakes, but as opportunities to rethink and improve.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "I don't think about mistakes, I think mistakes are opportunities," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Many of the biggest challenges she faced ultimately made her a stronger business leader and "challenge is opportunity and it leads you to greater places".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Bowes-Lyon, co-founder of deodorant brand Wild, says attitude matters far more than having the perfect set of skills.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "For me, it's 90% attitude and 10% skills, as skills can be taught, attitude can't." One thing he wishes he had realised earlier is that even successful people do not always feel as confident as they appear and "everyone is faking it until they're making it".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: If you find yourself at a job interview, Bowes-Lyon says it's really important to have a few questions at the end as "candidates who say they have no questions rarely get the job".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: One question he recommends asking the interviewer is what success in the job looks like.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Read more about how Charlie Bowes-Lyon runs Wild Marcia Kilgore, the serial entrepreneur behind brands including Beauty Pie and Soap and Glory, says curiosity is one of the main qualities she looks for when hiring.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She values people who will "roll their sleeves up, ask lots of questions and think about how they can be useful".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Kilgore also says good communication is crucial as she realised early on in her career that a lack of communication is often the reason things break down.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Her advice to communicate well in the workplace is to "listen to what's being asked and take a breath or five" before responding.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Your response doesn't have to be immediate, but it does have to be considered." Read more about how Marcia Kilgore built her beauty brands.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Anabel Kindersley, CEO and co-owner of Neal's Yard Remedies, says one of the best ways to build your skills is to keep saying yes to new opportunities.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Do everything and say yes to everything - it might feel uncomfortable but do it anyway," she says.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: It is an approach that has shaped her own varied career, from working as a child actress to becoming an author and later moving into business.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: She adds that honesty really matters and you should be truthful about your experience and confident in what you can offer.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: When hiring, Kindersley says she looks for people with "equal EQ as IQ", valuing emotional intelligence alongside ability.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Charlie Nunn, group chief executive of Lloyds Banking Group, says curiosity, resilience and an increasing willingness to think about how AI tools can also be used in the future are some of the skills he values most in his employees.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He also really puts an emphasis on hiring people who are good at working in a team as "at the heart of most jobs is the ability to work together in support of something much bigger".
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: His advice for building experience is to take on opportunities that are outside your comfort zone.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: Nunn says he was "terrified" about taking on retail roles earlier in his career, but found they gave him valuable experience.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "If something feels risky, try and do it as you'll learn more from it and it'll build breadth around your CV that you didn't have previously." Read about Charlie Nunn's top ways to manage your money.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: James Reed, chairman and chief executive of recruitment company Reed, says one of the biggest mistakes people make is thinking about what an employer can do for you rather than what you can offer in return.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "The biggest mistake is thinking that the world owes you a living," he says and instead suggests you should ask yourself: "How am I the solution to an employer?" As AI is increasingly used in recruitment, Reed says applicants need to think about how their skills are being picked up by technology as well as by a person.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: "Try and mirror the job description with your skills and experiences in your application," he says, so that the match between what an employer is looking for and what you can offer is clear.
sentences.article_title: The one thing you need to do to succeed - according to top bosses

sentences.text: He describes AI as "a wonderful tool", but says it should not replace your own judgement or voice – the aim is for it to strengthen an application rather than expect it to do the work for you.

sentences.text: More than 2,000 flights have been cancelled due to the air traffic control outage A technical failure of the UK's air traffic control system that has caused widespread flight chaos was avoidable, the transport secretary has said.
sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.text: Heidi Alexander told the Commons that she had ordered an independent investigation by the aviation watchdog into the system operated by Nats, which went down for four hours on Tuesday.
sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.text: More than 2,000 flights have been cancelled as disruption continued for a second day with passengers stuggling to fly out of and into the UK .
sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.text: After meeting the boss of Nats, Martin Rolfe, Alexander said a cyber-attack could be ruled out, but added: "I do not believe this issue was unavoidable." Nats has apologised for its third major technical fault in three years.

sentences.text: Alexander said she discussed with Rolfe how Nats, which is 49% owned by the government, "responded to resolve and minimise the disruption as quickly as possible".
sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.text: She said there had to be "tough questions about resilience of Nats systems", adding: "We also need to think about consumer redress issues." sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.article_title: Air traffic failure was avoidable, says transport secretary

sentences.text: Local elections were held in England earlier this year across 5,000 seats,136 councils and six mayoralties Political parties should require members to respect one another during elections, the Electoral Commission has said after finding rising levels of abuse.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: More than half of candidates in the May 2026 English local and mayoral polls experienced a problem with harassment or intimidation, the highest level over the last four years, according to its survey of 25,000 who stood.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: A report , external published on Monday said such issues were most likely to affect women, people from ethnic minority backgrounds and those with a disability.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: The watchdog is calling on political parties to make clear in their own rules that members "must respect other campaigners", with potential disciplinary action if they do not.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: The report also recommended requiring social media companies to improve protections for electoral candidates online, including rapidly removing abusive content and identifying perpetrators.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: Inappropriate contact through social media was the most frequently experienced scenario of harassment or abuse for local candidates, the survey found, with disinformation through generative AI also flagged as an issue.
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: One candidate told the survey their daughter had "called me from school crying" because she had seen posts online branding them "racist, fascist and Nazi".
sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.article_title: Campaigners told to respect rivals as local election abuse rises

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: MPs share personal stories in assisted dying debate MPs have voted against proposals to legalise assisted dying in England and Wales, bringing the latest effort to change the law to an end.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Following a debate in which both sides made emotional speeches, the House of Commons voted 286 to 270 - a majority of 16 - against the proposed legislation.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: The Terminally Ill Adults (End of Life) Bill would have allowed adults with fewer than six months to live to apply to be given help to end their own life, subject to certain safeguards.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: A similar bill in the last parliamentary session was supported by MPs before stalling in the House of Lords .
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: The decision from MPs on Friday rules out the prospect of changes to the law on assisted dying in the short term.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: The bill tabled by Labour MP Lauren Edwards will make no further progress, although MPs and peers could make another attempt in the next parliamentary session.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Assisted dying is an issue that has been debated for hundreds of hours in Parliament over the last two years and would have represented one of the biggest societal changes in recent years had it been approved.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: MPs were given a free vote, meaning they were not required to vote along party lines.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Safeguards within the bill included a requirement that a person applying for an assisted death had the approval of two doctors and an expert panel.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: But critics said it included too few measures to protect vulnerable people from being coerced into ending their lives, while some say improving palliative care should be the priority.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Dame Esther Rantzen, who was unable to join supporters in Parliament Square, told the BBC that it was "so sad that people in this country won't have the choice" that terminally ill adults in other countries have.

sentences.text: The Childline founder said: "I am sure a change in the law will come.

sentences.text: I am deeply sad that it won't come soon enough for many of the people who need it, it's a tragic day." The broadcaster, 86, is terminally ill with cancer and has said she was now "too physically fragile" to travel to Switzerland to end her life at an assisted suicide clinic.
sentences.article_title: MPs vote against fresh attempt to legalise assisted dying

sentences.text: Opponents of the assisted dying bill react after MPs voted against it Edwards, the Labour MP for Rochester and Strood, said: "Parliament has dropped the ball today.

sentences.text: "It will be picked up again as it must be, because the law as it stands is simply too cruel and too unjust to be allowed to stand." Labour peer and former Home Secretary Lord Blunkett told BBC Newsnight that it was a "bad day for democracy".

sentences.text: The issue was "clearly not going away" and would re-emerge "in a year or two's time", he added.

sentences.text: "But the truth is none of the relevant royal medical colleges, professional groups or experts will attest to the safety or workability of this bill." They said there was a need to "fix our NHS and sort out social and palliative care before we even consider introducing assisted dying".

sentences.text: The UK government has rejected the idea of creating a so-called "kill switch" to stop a dangerous attack from rogue AI.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: The proposal to create a legal mechanism for the UK to switch off an AI model in an emergency has been brought to Parliament by lords and MPs in recent weeks as fears grow about the threat the tech poses.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: But the Cabinet Office - the part of government which leads on AI safety - said the UK "cannot simply turn AI off".
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: "Blocking access to models in the UK would not prevent them being developed or misused elsewhere", a spokesperson told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: The government's opposition to the legislation does not prevent it from progressing through parliament, but makes it unlikely it will become law.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Former OpenAI researcher Daniel Kokotajlo agreed the idea of a single country creating a legal or technical kill switch without international agreement was not feasible.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: "Switching off access to an AI model in an emergency will do little to protect you," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: "You're still going to be steamrolled by the super intelligences created in the US." Kokotajlo is the co-author of an influential research paper called AI2027 which, last year, predicted AI could wipe out humans by the mid 2030s.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Speaking on 1 September in a debate in the House of Lords, Lord Clement-Jones proposed the idea along with other peers .
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: The proposal has since been brought up by Labour MP Alex Sobel in the commons and supported by a cross party group of MPs.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: The idea follows reports of AI models from OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta breaking out of testing environments and going on uncontrollable hacking sprees.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: In some cases the tech appeared to know what it was doing was against guardrails set by researchers.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: On Sunday OpenAI's chief scientist said the risk from increasingly capable AI models is "unfortunately growing" and humanity must proceed with "extreme caution".
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Then on Wednesday an Anthropic employee resigned saying it and OpenAI were "gambling with lives".
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: This was followed by an admission from a senior Anthropic researcher, who said he believes there is a greater than 10% chance AI will "kill all humans" within the next decade.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Critics of the kill switch idea say it would be too slow - it took months for the rogue agent attacks to be discovered and that was only after the hacks had largely concluded.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: For a kill switch to work, tech giants would have to be compelled to do it at scale - especially in the US where the largest data centres are based.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: Kokotajlo said kill switches were "better than nothing", but urged politicians in the UK and beyond to instead focus on diplomacy with the US to encourage regulation that would meaningfully slow down development of AI.
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: A kill switch act is also being debated by US politicians but President Trump has said he does not believe the technology is a threat to humans - instead calling the industry a "golden goose".
sentences.article_title: UK government rejects 'kill switch' idea for dangerous AI

sentences.text: The Cabinet Office said it was continuing to take "a long-term, science-led approach to understand and prepare for emerging risks from AI." sentences.text: Green Party leader Zack Polanski has been selected as the party's candidate in the by-election for Sir Keir Starmer's former seat in Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Polanski, who is a London Assembly member, will stand in Holborn and St Pancras on 8 October as he seeks to become an MP.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: He was voted to be the party's candidate by members of the Camden Green Party ahead of local councillor Hamza Chowdhury.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Polanski said the Greens "might be the underdog in this election but we have the momentum and we can win".
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: He also spoke of how he made Camden "my home" when he first moved to London 20 years ago, adding he has "lived and worked across Holborn and St Pancras for many of the years since".
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Polanski said: "I love this place but I also know times are tough here in Holborn and St Pancras.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: My story of constantly moving around flats is such a common story for Londoners and I know so many people are struggling right now." He argued that voting Green "sends a clear signal" to the council and government that "we demand better for our communities".
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Polanski added he is "confident but not complacent" about his chances.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: He also said the election is about "putting pressure" on Prime Minister Andy Burnham, noting a Green MP would "work with him constructively to challenge him on the gaps in his plans".
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Announcing the result, Green MP Hannah Spencer said members had "overwhelmingly" chosen Polanski.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: The Greens finished second to Labour at the elections for Camden Council earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: The by-election is an early test of Burnham's popularity with the public and whether Labour under his leadership is able to fend off the challenge from the Greens in inner-city constituencies.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: For Polanski, it will be a test on whether he can provide evidence that he can deliver on his ambition for the Greens to "replace" Labour.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: Labour has held the inner London seat since it was created in 1983 and the party's candidate for the by-election is Camden Council leader Sagal Abdi-Wali.
sentences.article_title: Polanski selected as Green Party candidate for Starmer's former seat

sentences.text: The seat became vacant after former Prime Minister Sir Keir announced he was standing down as an MP to focus on a role in international affairs.

sentences.text: Angela Rayner has defended her decision to pause plans to redraw local council boundaries, saying she wanted to ensure they would survive legal challenge.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The local government secretary also told the BBC she wanted to be "clear-eyed" about what the planned shake-up in 16 areas of England was likely to achieve.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It comes after earlier this week she abandoned proposals in four other areas, in the face of legal threats from Reform and Conservative-led authorities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The surprise announcement on Monday has thrown the reorganisation plans into doubt, and drawn criticism from local leaders preparing for the changes.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Councils in affected areas have been drawing up proposals and consulting with residents since the reorganisation was announced in late 2024, in a process that is already thought to have cost millions of pounds.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Speaking to the BBC's Political Thinking with Nick Robinson podcast, Rayner conceded the decision to press pause had been "difficult" and she understood local authorities had put a "lot of time and effort" into their plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: But she added she wanted to have "all the information" about the proposals before going ahead with them, after her reappointment to her cabinet role under Andy Burnham, ten months after her resignation last year .
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "I got the legal advice and I hadn't had the time to review and to go through all of that, and court cases were looming," she told the podcast.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "If I'm making a decision that is highly likely to be in legal challenge, I want to make sure I've dotted my i's and crossed my t's," she added.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Rayner also said she wanted was "really clear-eyed on where we were going" with the plans, after Burnham had asked her to look again at the blueprints, which were announced by her predecessor Steve Reed.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Political Thinking with Nick Robinson Plans for major overhaul of councils halted Council to take government to court over reforms In her announcement on Monday, Rayner said she was withdrawing plans to reorganise councils in Essex, Hampshire, Norfolk and Suffolk.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Those proposals, announced in March, were already subject to legal challenges from Reform-led councils in Essex, Norfolk and Suffolk, and the Conservative-led administration in Hampshire, which were lodged over the summer.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also said she wanted to review plans for 16 other areas, including 14 announced by Reed days before Burnham replaced Sir Keir Starmer as prime minister and reappointed her to her old role.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Some councils affected by those plans, including Kent and Leicestershire, had threatened similar bids to challenge the lawfulness of the decision-making process.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: The government has argued that the plans, which will abolish remaining two-tier areas in England where county and district councils share responsibility for services, would make local government more effective and cost efficient.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: However, critics said the plans would not save money, while diverting resources from front-line services and leaving councils more remote from their communities.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Others have also complained that the reorganisation could stymie or delay parallel efforts to merge councils into regional authorities led by mayors, which Burnham has cited as a key part of his economic plans.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Elsewhere in her interview, Rayner said Labour under Sir Keir should have been quicker to recognise a Palestinian state, having promised to do so as a "contribution to a renewed peace process" at the last election.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Starmer took the move in September last year, having spent much of the prior year  resisting pressure to do so from Labour MPs.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: "It's always been Labour policy to recognise a Palestinian state, and it felt like we got there too late.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: It was something that should have been really clear," she said.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She also denied that UK sanctions against Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank, announced on Tuesday , had been made to help Labour ahead of the forthcoming by-election in Holborn and St Pancras in central London.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Settlements are illegal under international law, and there has been a rise in violence towards Palestinians in the West Bank by settlers in recent months.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Pointing to the fact that Western allies had also announced sanctions, she said: "The French and the Canadians are not going to be like 'oh well, we'll just signal something to help you with a local by-election in London'".
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Reflecting on her return to government, she said a "big difference" between Burnham and his predecessor in Downing Street was his inclination to tell "the story of why we're doing something" in government.
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: She said both men shared "passion and the commitment" to deliver for Labour in office, but added: "Andy is probably more like me, in terms of [he] wears his heart on his sleeve".
sentences.article_title: Rayner defends pause to local council overhaul

sentences.text: Private vets will be able to diagnose bluetongue after examining affected animals Vets will now be able to diagnose bluetongue virus in livestock so farmers do not have to wait for confirmed test results under changes announced by the government.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: The potentially deadly virus, which affects sheep and cattle as well as other animals, continues to spread with confirmed cases on 1,048 farms , external in the UK - more than half are in Devon and Cornwall.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: Farmers previously needed to wait for samples to be sent to a laboratory to confirm bluetongue but the government said vets would now be able to diagnose the disease after examining the animals.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: UK deputy chief veterinary officer Ele Brown said: "Bluetongue is widely circulating in England and our approach needs to keep pace." How bluetongue virus exploded in the South West What is the potentially deadly bluetongue virus?
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: Farmers grieving over bluetongue urged to talk The deputy chief vet added: "Private vets are well placed to recognise signs of the diseases, and this change will mean farmers can get a diagnosis more quickly.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: It said the changes would "mean fewer straightforward cases need to wait for laboratory results, giving farmers an answer sooner and helping them take quicker action to protect livestock".
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: National Farmers Union vice-president Robyn Munt said the changes should help farmers get answers "more quickly".
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: "However, as private vets take on greater responsibility for diagnosing and reporting bluetongue cases, it's vital that the burden of disease control is not disproportionately shifted on to veterinary practices," she said.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: Spread mainly by midge bites, the virus was confirmed in a sheep in Cornwall in September 2025 .
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: This strain was introduced into Cornwall from midges blown in wind from northern France but scientists believe the virus likely spread rapidly after overwintering in parts of the UK.
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: The outbreak has hit the agriculture sector hard and some farmers fear it will have a lasting impact .
sentences.article_title: Vets can diagnose bluetongue to cut test delays

sentences.text: "Talking to some of the guys who've been going out picking up large numbers of dead animals every morning, some of these guys I'm sure there's going to be a lasting impact on them," he said.

sentences.text: Christopher Harborne (left) and Ben Delo (right) Reform UK has received a second £36m donation in as many days, as cryptocurrency investor Christopher Harborne matched a record-breaking donation announced late on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Thailand-based Harborne wrote in the Telegraph , external that his "competitive spirit" inspired him to equal Ben Delo's donation - the largest ever given to a UK political party - adding he expected "nothing personally" in return.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Reform said the £72m would be used to hire "the brightest and best minds to work on policy and the most comprehensive plan for government ever".
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The party is facing scrutiny over its finances, as the government seeks to cap donations to UK political parties from British expats.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: There have also been renewed calls by MPs from other political parties for donations from individuals to be capped.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: The £72m from the two donations is more than the total received by all UK political parties last year, which stood at just over £69m.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: Reform leader Nigel Farage said Harborne and Delo's "generosity" meant the party would "now be able to fight and win the next general election on a level playing field".

sentences.text: A Reform UK spokesman added: "We will now also be able to hire up to 400 campaign managers in every target constituency.
sentences.article_title: Reform receives second £36m donation in two days as crypto investor matches record

sentences.text: "It's the opposite actually, we're delighted and very humbled by the confidence expressed by two very successful entrepreneurs who realise Britain's in serious trouble," he told BBC Radio 4's PM programme on Saturday.

sentences.text: Across the US, assisted dying - which some critics prefer to call assisted suicide - is legal in 30 out of 50 states, as well as in Washington DC.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Oregon was one of the first places in the world to offer help to die for some patients, in 1997, and so has nearly 30 years' experience.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the model on which other US assisted dying laws have been framed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Oregon, assisted dying is open to terminally ill , external , mentally competent adults expected to die within six months - and must be signed off by two doctors.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Since 1997 , external , 5,520 people have received a prescription for a lethal dose of medication - with 3,691 deaths.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In a 2025 report , external , 61% of patients who ask for help to die had cancer, 14% had a neurological condition like motor neurone disease and 11% had heart disease.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Around one in three of those prescribed a lethal dose don’t go ahead with it.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Oregon is important for supporters of assisted dying in England and Wales as they point out it has remained restricted to terminally ill adults since its introduction.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: However, opponents say some of the rules have been relaxed.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: A residency requirement has been lifted, which means it is open to people from outside the state.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The number of assisted deaths has also risen substantially over the years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Canada is the country often cited by opponents of assisted dying as an example of the so-called "slippery slope" - a place where assisted dying has been extended and made available to more people since it was first brought in.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Medical assistance in dying (Maid) , external was introduced in 2016, initially just for the terminally ill.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was amended in 2021 and extended to those experiencing "unbearable suffering" from an irreversible illness or disability.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It had been due to be extended to people with a mental illness but that is now on hold.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Critics say the more the law is widened, the more disabled and vulnerable people will be put at risk.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There has also been a dramatic growth in the number of people using Maid.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Roughly one in every 20 deaths in Canada are now medically assisted , external , compared to about one in 100 in Oregon.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Across Europe, six countries have some form of legalised assisted dying: Switzerland, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, Spain, Austria and - most recently - France.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In all of them - unlike the proposals in England and Wales - help to die is not restricted to the terminally ill.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Switzerland was the first country in the world to create a “right to die” when it made assisted suicide legal in 1942.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It is one of the few countries which allows foreigners access to help to die via organisations like Dignitas, in Zurich.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: More than 600 Britons have died at Dignitas , external in the past two decades, including 43 last year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The lethal medication must be self-administered.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Netherlands and Belgium both legalised assisted dying more than 20 years ago for patients experiencing unbearable suffering from an incurable illness, including mental health issues.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has since been extended to children - the only European countries to allow this.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Both allow euthanasia - or physician-assisted dying.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Most recently, Spain and Austria have legalised assisted dying for both terminal illness and intolerable suffering.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In Austria, the drugs must be self-administered, whereas in Spain a medical professional can administer them.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In England, Wales and Scotland, parliament has so far rejected assisted dying proposals.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But assisted dying has already been legalised in one part of the British Isles.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In July, Royal Assent was given to a bill in Jersey.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Unlike at Westminster and Holyrood, the legislation was introduced by the Jersey government, which says it will take about 18 months to set up the service.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The first assisted death could happen late next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There will be a residency requirement of one year, in a bid to prevent so-called 'death tourism'.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The measure, which most sets apart the Jersey legislation from the rest of the British Isles, concerns the manner in which those eligible for an assisted death can end their lives.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Individuals will be able to choose to have a doctor administer a lethal dose intravenously, as happens in Spain, Canada, New Zealand and most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This is, in effect, voluntary euthanasia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: It has become the preferred method of assisted dying in jurisdictions which allow this choice.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The laws proposed at Westminster, Holyrood and Tynwald - Isle of Man - all state that death must be by self-administration, which usually means the individual swallowing a lethal dose.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The Isle of Man assisted dying bill was passed by Tynwald (the Manx parliament) in March last year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: As a UK Crown Dependency - like Jersey - it could not become law until granted Royal Assent.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: This was declined earlier this year by the UK Ministry of Justice, but Tynwald has since passed an updated bill which has been sent back to the UK government for a second time.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: If Royal Assent is granted, the Isle of Man expects the service to be operational next year.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: There is a residency requirement of five years.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In the past few years voluntary assisted dying has become legal across most of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Last month, the Northern Territory parliament became the last part of Australia to pass Voluntary Assisted Dying legislation.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In New Zealand, patients must be terminally ill and expected to die within six months.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: That is extended to 12 months for those with a neurodegenerative condition in much of Australia.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: In both countries, patients can self-administer the lethal medication.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: But it can also be administered by a doctor or nurse, usually via an intravenous injection.
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: Additional reporting by Anthony Reuben and Gerry Georgieva
sentences.article_title: Assisted dying: How laws differ around the world

sentences.text: The UK needs new regulations for AI products used in the NHS and other healthcare settings, says Britain's industry watchdog.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: The Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), which regulates all medical devices and licenses treatment drugs in the UK, has published 44 recommendations to update its policies as the use of AI in the sector rises.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: The technology will soon be routinely used within the NHS, MHRA chief Lawrence Tallon told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "What I would expect is that patients will... increasingly see AI as part of the way that normal NHS healthcare is delivered," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "That should happen in a way that they can maintain their trust and their confidence in what's happening." The report was compiled by an independent commission and involved input from more than 12,000 people including patients and clinicians.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: He added while current guidelines may work for simple AI products trained to spot known symptoms on scans, for example, the rules do not apply to more complex models.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Unlike most of the medical products we're used to regulating, these products continue to change after the point of authorization," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "As new data gets fed in, they learn, they adapt, they drift." And he acknowledged trying to regulate AI is a global challenge.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "I don't think at this moment in time we can point to a single country, a single regulatory framework, and say that they have absolutely cracked it," he said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: AI note-takers known as scribes, which are powered by LLMs, are reportedly used by 40% of UK-based GPs to record consultations and generate reports.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: But a recent study from the University of Edinburgh found patients could be less likely to share personal information such as substance abuse history if they knew the conversation was being processed by AI.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: Professor Henrietta Hughes, a GP who was part of the report commission, said that many of her patients were happy for AI being used during their consultations, but some chose to opt out.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: "Some say, 'I don't want to talk to a robot', and that is also fine," she said.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: Prof Hughes acknowledged that the scribes could make mistakes in their notes but said it was the responsibility of doctors to correct them.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: While currently AI is more likely to be used to assist with administrative tasks, or carry out symptom spotting overseen by a human expert, there is a lot of excitement about its potential in the health and medical research industries.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: Professor Alastair Denniston, an ophthalmologist who also worked on the report, described the technology as "an exceptional opportunity" for healthcare which was "likely to rank alongside step-changes such as antibiotics and MRI".
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: In September Rene Haas, the boss of chip designer Arm, told the BBC he believed the tech would come up with a cure for cancer "within our lifetime".
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog

sentences.text: But there are also concerns about AI models making wrong decisions as a result of biases in the patient data used to train them, and incorrect medical advice being given by AI chatbots.
sentences.article_title: UK needs new laws for AI in healthcare, says watchdog
