sentences.text: Alan is one of thousands each month who are not being treated within the cancer target timeframe Alan was diagnosed with lung cancer after a nodule was found in June last year.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: The 70-year-old was meant to be operated on within weeks but ended up waiting nearly five months, by which time the cancer had spread, making his surgery more complex.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "I was so frustrated and angry and couldn't understand why they would leave me like that," says Alan.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: On two occasions, scans were cancelled because machines had broken and for weeks he heard little or nothing from the hospital about when he would eventually have the urgent surgery.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Alan is one of thousands each month in England who are not being treated within the target timeframe.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Earlier this year, the government's National Cancer Plan, along with the NHS Planning Guidance, set out that 80% of patients in England would start treatment within 62 days from urgent GP referral by March 2027.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: This was to reach 85% by March 2029.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: But in the months since the government announced this ambition, performance has got worse, according to NHS England data, not better.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Now, 71.2% of patients start cancer treatment within the 62 day timeframe.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Prof Pat Price, a leading UK clinical academic oncologist, says the government targets "are now simply impossible to hit", after what she describes as a "complete loss of momentum".
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Price attributes the current failures to a "complete lack of a plan or accountability".
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: The plan stated that a new independent cancer board would be established, but it is still not known who will be leading this group.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: NHS data released on Thursday, for July, reveals 10 out of 120 hospital trusts in England managed to get 85% of patients to start treatment within 62 of their urgent referral by a GP.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Radiotherapy UK analysis, shared exclusively with the BBC, suggests more than 2,800 extra patients would need to start treatment every month - a near 15% increase on current numbers - to achieve the March 2027 target.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: That is likely to grow as referrals keep rising across nearly every cancer type.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Price says thousands of patients "are going to die unnecessarily, just because the government can't get their act together to treat people on time".
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: For every month a cancer patient waits before starting treatment, their chance of survival falls by around 10%, on average.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: By the time Alan had his operation, the cancer had spread to his lymph nodes and the nodule "had grown at an alarming rate", according to the lung specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: He has since been told the cancer has cleared awaiting his one-year review, but the operation has left him in debilitating pain.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "I used to play golf and get out and about.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Now I can't do any of the things I love," says Alan.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Roughly 54,000 more patients will need to start treatment within 62 days before 2029 for the government to hit its goal.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: One NHS trust that is gaining traction on its waiting list numbers is Salisbury, but it is still not hitting targets.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Staff say there is no single fix, just a relentless focus on getting the basics right; making sure patients know about their appointments and turn up, keeping IT systems working, recruiting the right people, making sure surgical lists are full and expanding capacity.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Much of the visible progress has come through skin and prostate cancer, two of the most common cancers in the country.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Diane had a cancerous lump removed from her face at Salisbury District Hospital a few weeks ago, using an innovative procedure, which checks tumour margins are clear while the patient is still in surgery.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: That means no follow-up operations, and it allows for complex reconstruction that leaves hardly a trace.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "It's amazing, you literally can't see I had a large cancerous lesion removed from my cheek," she tells the BBC in the waiting room.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Consultant plastic surgeon Neil Wickham checked her face, confirmed a biopsied lump on her arm was benign, and referred her to ENT for a separate lump in her neck.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: It is the kind of joined-up care the government's Cancer Plan was meant to trigger in cancer units across England.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Diane benefited from an innovative procedure when she had a cancerous lump removed from her face But over in pathology at the Salisbury trust, head of department Lee Phillips is feeling the pressure.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: His histology lab receives cancer service biopsies from across the hospital for diagnosis.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "The sheer volume of specimens we have coming in is our problem," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "We need more staff and more kit if we're going to keep up with demand," Phillips says.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Radiotherapy is another bottleneck crying out for staff and kit.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Like many trusts, Salisbury has no machine on site, so patients needing daily sessions over one to three weeks must travel up to an hour to Southampton, and sometimes Bath.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: But staff in Salisbury also say missed appointments, whether down to late letters, illness, transport problems or anxiety, are a constant drain on a system already stretched thin.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Emilia Scutt, cancer manager in Salisbury, says that efforts to reduce missed appointments have really helped their numbers.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Rising demand, workforce shortages and diagnostic bottlenecks have all played a part.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: Some pointed to industrial action and staff sickness, others to reliance on outside diagnostic providers or major changes to how their systems work.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: All say they are investing in extra capacity, working through backlogs and redesigning pathways, and are already seeing early signs of improvement.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: "If government is serious about delivering on the ambitions of the National Cancer Plan for England, it must match ambition with urgency," said Steve Haines of Macmillan Cancer Support.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: He said that "visible progress" was needed on a promise to set up a National Cancer Board to oversee progress on improving waiting times and treatment.
sentences.article_title: 'My cancer spread while I waited months for surgery': The cost of England's cancer wait times

sentences.text: A Department of Health and Social Care spokesperson says "cancer waiting times are moving in the right direction will all three cancer standards better than a year ago".

sentences.text: People will be able to go to their local chemist in England this autumn and get on-the-spot treatment for 12 common conditions without going to their GP first.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Pharmacists can already prescribe medication for seven conditions -  sore throat, earache, sinusitis, shingles, impetigo, infected bites and urinary tract infections.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Five more - migraines, acne, scabies, ear infections and badly blocked noses - are now also being added to that list.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: NHS England said the move was to ease pressure on busy GPs and A&E departments while making sure people could get treatment quickly and conveniently.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: After a very hot summer and three of the busiest months on record in A&Es in England, the NHS says it wants to make it as easy as possible for people to get help when they need it for everyday conditions.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham said people were "fed up with the scramble for routine appointments" and wanted help close to home, with no more taking time off work or waiting to get seen.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "For five more common conditions, you'll be able to walk into your local pharmacy and get treated on the spot," he said.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Mr Burnham said families would feel the change, and the plan would give people back "precious time".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: There will be a gradual rollout and the service will eventually be available at thousands of community NHS pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Community pharmacies also offer support with healthy eating, exercise, stopping smoking, monitoring your blood pressure, contraception, flu and Covid vaccinations.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: The charity the Migraine Trust said it was delighted by the news after calling for more help for migraine care in pharmacies.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Chief executive Rob Music said having this support for people with migraine through their local pharmacy was "a wonderful opportunity for a faster and improved care pathway".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: Dr Amanda Doyle, director for primary care and community services at NHS England, said she wanted to make sure that patients can get as much support as possible in their communities, "so they do not have to be admitted to hospital unnecessarily".
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: But bodies representing pharmacies across England have consistently said that the funding provided by the goverment does not cover the workload for the new plans.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "Pharmacies are still under significant financial pressures," said Henry Gregg, chief executive of the National Pharmacy Association.
sentences.article_title: Migraines and acne among five more conditions pharmacists can treat

sentences.text: "This shows why the government should go much further and invest in our pharmacy network that has the power to transform people's experience of everyday health issues." The Pharmacy First scheme started in England in 2024.

sentences.text: Lynn said she had lost trust in Addenbrooke's Hospital, where her daughter Tammy underwent surgery A mum whose daughter was among more than 200 patients "harmed" after being operated on by a now-suspended NHS surgeon says she has lost trust in the hospital that treated her.

sentences.text: Of the 209 patients who "experienced harm" under the care of orthopaedic surgeon Kuldeep Stohr at Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge, 41 were classed as severe and one person died, as first reported by the BBC on Monday.
sentences.article_title: Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital

sentences.text: Lynn, whose 13-year-old daughter Tammy was among the first to receive findings from an independent investigation last year, said the number of patients involved was "ridiculous".
sentences.article_title: Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital

sentences.text: The hospital trust said it was "deeply sorry".
sentences.article_title: Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital

sentences.text: Stohr previously said she was fully co-operating with an investigation.
sentences.article_title: Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital

sentences.text: Kuldeep Stohr is being investigated in relation to hundreds of operations An ongoing review by the Cambridge University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (CUH) has looked into the care of more than 900 patients so far.
sentences.article_title: Mum 'lost trust' in surgeon review hospital

sentences.text: Protesters demonstrating against benefit cuts at a rally in Parliament Square in 2025 Support for disability benefits remains "remarkably strong" and cutting them would be "politically risky" according to a new report.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The analysis, from the British Social Attitudes survey, found that fewer than one in 10 people favoured cutting welfare payments for the disabled, with almost half of people saying they would support more being spent on them, even if it led to higher taxes.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The report comes amid mounting concerns among several political parties about the growing cost of disability benefits.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Spending on the main disability benefit is forecast to more than double in a decade, reaching £41bn by 2030.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: But the report says that cutting these payments would not be easy.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: "Despite growing political divisions on welfare, support for disability benefits remains remarkably strong," said Dr Robert de Vries from the University of Kent, who was one of the report's co-authors.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: "Very few people favour cuts, disabled people are seen as among the most deserving recipients of support, and proposals to reduce disability benefits appear politically risky across the political spectrum." The analysis is based on 4,656 interviews gathered between August and October 2025.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The authors noted that the timing of the interviews, just after the Sir Keir Starmer's government had failed to reform PIP, meant it was "possible that people were particularly supportive of disability benefits at the time".
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: They cautioned that public attitudes to disability benefits "crucially depend on which disabled people are in the public's mind", referencing previous research that showed that "some types of disabled people are seen as 'deserving' by the public".
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The findings come despite the proportion of those who support increasing welfare spending for the poor being at a near record low.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Labour, the Conservative party and Reform UK have all said there is a need to reduce the amount of money being spent on health and disability benefits, while the Liberal Democrats, Greens and SNP oppose reductions.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Efforts by Sir Keir to introduce cuts last year were opposed by many in his own party, forcing a government climbdown .
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The proportion of GDP the UK spends on all welfare benefits for those of working age has remained broadly flat over the past 40 years, at just under 5%.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Asked if "the government should spend more money on welfare benefits for the poor, even if it leads to higher taxes," 27% replied they should while 42% were opposed.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: The latest figures show four million people in England and Wales are currently in receipt of Personal Independence Payment (PIP), the main disability benefit.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Just 7% were in favour of cutting such benefits for disabled people who cannot work.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: A majority also strongly backed extra payments for the costs of having a disability.
sentences.article_title: Support for disability benefits 'remarkably strong' report finds

sentences.text: Sarah Mackay, known as @fitwsarah online, says her energy levels change through her cycle A woman points to a colour-coded grid dividing the menstrual cycle into four phases, each paired with a different list of exercises.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "When you're bleeding, you want to be doing steady-pace jogging, Pilates, barre, walking, resting," she tells viewers.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This is one of thousands of videos on TikTok and Instagram suggesting that people change their workouts depending on where they are in their menstrual cycles - something known as 'cycle-syncing'.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: So-called cycle-syncing workout plans have surged in popularity online, with Google searches for the term rising 740% since 2022 and more than 55,000 TikTok videos now using the #cyclesyncing hashtag.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Most of the advice is shared by fitness and wellness creators rather than medical or research experts.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Kelly McNulty, a researcher at Leeds Beckett University specialising in menstrual cycles and exercise, says there is evidence that some women experience changes in symptoms, energy or perceived strength across their cycle.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But that is different from evidence that all women should train in a particular way at a particular point, she tells the BBC, adding that these videos are "a trend based on marketing rather than any kind of research or evidence".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "There isn't any research to support that kind of phase-based prescription," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: This video can not be played Should you sync your exercise routine with your period?
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: A key issue is that menstrual cycles are highly individual, McNulty adds - they can differ between women, and one woman's experience can also change from one cycle to the next.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: That makes the blanket advice often found on social media difficult to apply, she explains.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Many cycle-tracking apps and programmes are also designed around relatively regular menstrual cycles that are 21 to 35 days, which can make their recommendations less applicable to people with irregular periods, or those using hormonal contraception.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She doesn't follow a prescriptive plan, she says, but instead makes changes intuitively.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my luteal phase I'll try and ease off in the training," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "In my follicular phase, I'm so energised, I feel like I can lift so much heavier.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: I like to try and get my long runs in." Burgoyne also welcomes the growing attention on women's health, and says that exercise and nutrition research has historically focused heavily on male bodies, with findings then often applied to women.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Sarah says she has sometimes hit personal records while on her period Fitness creator Sarah Mackay, known as @liftwsarah on Instagram and TikTok, has also noticed her energy, motivation, cramps and mood change through the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: But she deliberately avoids strict plans because, she says, "there are too many variables at play".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Some online plans advise women to avoid intense training during their period, she says, yet she has sometimes hit personal records while menstruating.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "The problem is not that the menstrual cycle is irrelevant," she says, but that "not everything is predictable".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Dr Faye Bate, a trained medical doctor and women's health expert, is also wary of advice suggesting all women should train differently according to their menstrual phase.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: "A one-size-fits-all model of 'you should be exercising this way in this phase and a different way in a different phase' shouldn't be advice that applies to all women," she says.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: She is concerned that repeatedly telling women they are likely to be weaker or less capable at particular points in their cycle could create a "nocebo" effect - where negative expectations themselves influence how someone feels or performs.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty tells the BBC that routinely easing off resistance training could also limit progress.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Strength training is particularly important for women, who face a higher risk of osteoporosis later in life.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: While cycle-syncing itself may not be backed by strong evidence, the experts we spoke to did suggest being "cycle-aware".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: McNulty says tracking your cycle can be a useful way to understand your own patterns, while Dr Bate also encourages women to become more familiar with how they feel at different points in the month.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Both welcome the fact that menstrual health is being discussed more openly, but say the focus should be on individual experience, rather than rigid, phase-based rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In practice, that might mean having painkillers ready before your period, taking a rest day when symptoms are worse, or easing off a workout if you feel unusually fatigued.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: For Dr Bate, "the most important part is tuning in to how you feel".
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: In other words, use your cycle as information rather than a set of rules.
sentences.article_title: Menstrual fitness: Why some women are 'cycle-syncing' their workouts

sentences.text: Have you ever slept next to a snoring partner and woken up feeling stressed, unfocused or forgetful the next day?
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: As snoring is relatively common, it is often left untreated and dismissed as a harmless irritation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But according to experts, sleeping next to a snorer could be impacting your health.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Snoring is caused by the vibration of the soft tissues in our upper airways during sleep, explains Dr Clare Simon, a dentist with a special interest in dental sleep medicine.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: About 40% of the UK adult population snores, with the issue affecting more men than women, says the British Snoring and Sleep Apnoea Association (BSSAA).
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: And 75% of people with a snoring partner say they have had their sleep impacted, according to a US survey by the Sleep Foundation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Here's what you need to know about the impact on partners - and what you can do about it.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Prof Ama Johal, a consultant orthodontist and sleep expert at Aerox Health, explains that the partner of a snorer can become "so impacted upon that it's almost a last-ditch effort on their part to get up and go sleep in a separate room because they have to sleep".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: He adds: "As humans we physically can't function without that necessity." Prof Ama Johal says many couples put up with the negative effects snoring for too long During the night, we cycle through different stages of sleep in repeating patterns, usually every 90 minutes.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: The deeper stages of this cycle are important for physical restoration.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If sleep is frequently disrupted, you may spend less time in the restorative stages, meaning you can wake up feeling tired, even if you've spent a lot of time in bed, the BSSAA explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Your brain processes and stores information from the day during sleep.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Fragmented sleep - which can happen if you're waking up due to a snoring partner - can interrupt this process, impacting your focus and memory.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Disrupted sleep can also impact hormone regulation, which affects your energy levels and motivation.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Sleep also plays a role in regulating the brain systems involved in stress and emotional response.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: When it is disrupted, these systems can become less balanced, which may make you feel more irritable and less able to cope with stress.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: This is something Meg Warren, 29, experienced when her former partner's snoring would keep her up.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says: "Without fail, after a snoring-induced wake up I would feel on incredibly high alert." Meg, a charity media officer, would prod him throughout the night and try to coax him from his back to his side.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: She says she would wake up "feeling groggy and dazed, sometimes so much so that it would feel like a hangover".
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Meg Warren felt 'groggy and dazed' after a night of little sleep due to her former partner's snoring Anna-Louise Dearden, a 52-year-old journalist, says she sometimes sleeps in a separate room from her partner due to his snoring.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Having this option allows her to prioritise getting enough rest when the snoring is particularly bad.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: There are things that can be done, say both Simon and Johal.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: But first, it is important to distinguish whether your partner is simply snoring, or whether they have sleep apnoea.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: "What you don't want to do is simply make someone quieter at night while potentially missing an underlying sleep-related breathing disorder," Simon says.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Signs of sleep apnoea, a disorder that causes a person's breathing to repeatedly stop and start during sleep, include pauses in breathing, choking at night, waking frequently, and suffering from morning headaches.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: If this is what you are dealing with, you could be recommended a Continuous Positive Airway Pressure (CPAP) machine, or even surgical treatment in some cases, Simon explains.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: For simple snoring, Simon said that lifestyle changes can make a difference, such as losing weight, stopping smoking, reducing alcohol intake before bed, or changing your sleeping position - such as laying on your side rather than your back.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: You can also suggest to your partner that they see a GP, who will be able to advise further or refer you to a specialist.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: An expert might suggest treating nasal obstruction or allergies, if this is what is causing snoring, or wearing a custom mouthguard to gently push the lower jaw forward and keep the airway open.
sentences.article_title: 'Like a hangover': Why your partner's snoring could be impacting your health

sentences.text: Johal says too many couples put up with snoring "for too long", which impacts their relationships and wellbeing.

sentences.text: Sleep scores, magnesium, white noise machines - what was once the simple act of sleeping has become a minefield.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Trying to optimise sleep in this way is called "sleepmaxxing".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Take it too far, and you could end up with "orthosomnia" - the clinical term for an obsession with achieving perfect sleep.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: While it's not formally recognised as a condition in the UK, doctors tell the BBC they've noticed signs of orthosomnia in their patients, with some bringing their sleep tracker data into appointments convinced, wrongly, that they have a sleep disorder.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: That fixation is actually making people's sleep worse, they warn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: So how and why did sleep become so complicated?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: And if sleepmaxxing isn't the answer, what is the elusive secret to a good night's sleep?
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The first commercial fitness tracker to incorporate sleep analysis was the Fitbit Classic in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Since then, many others - including Garmin, Whoop and Apple - have integrated sleep trackers into wrist-worn devices, as have smart rings such as Oura, Ultrahuman and RingConn.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: These devices vary, but in general they all provide users with a report of their night, broken down by sleep stages - time awake, light sleep, deep sleep, and REM (rapid eye movement).
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Many also give users a "sleep score".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: But the concept of a sleep score is "completely made up", according to Dr Alanna Hare, consultant of sleep medicine at the Royal Brompton Hospital in London.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "There's nothing recognised in sleep science that is a 'sleep score'," she tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "That's just been created by manufacturers." This video can not be played How sleep-tracking can make your sleep worse Hare says she's noticed trackers causing anxiety among her patients.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I've noticed more patients coming to me with data from various trackers, with lots of questions about sleep that... is probably contributing to their sleep difficulties," she says.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Even though some have had medical tests with reassuring results, this hasn't allayed their fears, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "It's great that there's more focus on sleep as part of wellness," she adds.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "But sleep just does not respond well to attempts to perfect it." One proposed lawsuit against Oura, filed last month in San Francisco, alleges that Oura rings are unable to accurately measure sleep quality and sleep stages, and instead rely on AI-generated estimates that have "a coin flip's chance of being correct".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In response, Oura told the BBC that it "stand[s] behind our science, research and accuracy claims".
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "We're committed to clearly communicating what Oura measures, what it estimates, and how members should use that information," the company added.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Studies also show sleep trackers can affect how you function during the day, even if they're not accurate.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: In one study , external from the University of Oxford, participants were given sleep trackers which assigned them a sleep score.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The scores were randomised, however, and had no relation to how the participants had actually slept.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: The next day participants rated their mood, fatigue levels and alertness, before tests checking their focus and reaction times.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: Researchers found that the people told they'd slept badly reported feeling more fatigued, and were less mentally alert - even though the sleep scores were all fake.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: This is something Jess Hill says she noticed in herself after getting a Garmin watch several years ago.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I started to rely on the watch as my Bible for whether I slept well or not," the 32-year-old HR professional from London tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "I would think, 'I've had awful sleep so I'm going to really struggle today', even if I actually probably had okay sleep.

sentences.text: "The thing with tracking your sleep is that it gives you a number, and this means you have a target," he tells the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Why 'sleepmaxxing' could be making your sleep worse

sentences.text: "So you get into this cycle of worrying about your quality of sleep or the quantity of sleep based on figures." He says he carried out research into actigraphy - wrist-worn sleep trackers - around 40 years ago.

sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hyaluronic acid is a naturally occurring sugar molecule in the body and is known as a "moisture magnet" as it grabs hold of water.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Dr Javed Hussain performs a range of cosmetic procedures, including penis fillers Dr Javed Hussain has been offering penis fillers for more than a year at his clinic in Prestwich, Greater Manchester.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain trained as a doctor before moving into cosmetic procedures, but penis fillers do not legally require any medical training to perform.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He says demand is increasing.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He's treated men of all ages - some in their mid-20s, while his oldest client is aged 72.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The process starts with consultations on the patient's health, reasons for wanting to have the procedure, expectations about the results, and a discussion about the risks.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: On the day of the event itself, a penis is injected with hyaluronic acid three times - on the top and on either side.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The hyaluronic acid filler is delivered through a cannula that enters at the base and travels along the length of the shaft.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The equipment needed, including cannulas and syringe, to perform a penis filler procedure The filler is then massaged to give an even look, which the patient continues at home.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: At a cost of up to £3,500, Hussain says men can expect between 10% and 20% more girth for the next six to nine months.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: These range from relatively minor ones such as soreness, bruising and uneven filler, to serious ones including infection.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: These risks apply to all procedures using filler.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: However, there is also a risk of damaging the vital structures and blood vessels in the penis that are needed for an erection.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: When asked why he feels comfortable offering procedures that are concerning surgeons, Hussain says he "totally understands" why some are worried.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "It comes from the right place, that nervousness," he says, "but at the same time, more and more evidence is growing and we're getting the results" and that "there is a benefit" to men.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Hussain says he has an "immediate action plan" including drugs to quickly dissolve the filler in the event that things go wrong, and reports that "thankfully, we've never needed to" - although the BBC cannot independently corroborate that.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But he recalls one patient who came to him for advice after treatment elsewhere, which had "really gone wrong".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He says the incorrect type of filler had been used and the "shaft of the penis was starting to become black" as the procedure had damaged the blood vessels in the penis and the skin was dying.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: The man was sent straight to A&E.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Prof Vaibhav Modgil has seen men for whom penis enhancement procedures have gone wrong Prof Vaibhav Modgil, an andrologist and consultant urological surgeon for the NHS in Manchester, has seen these men coming into hospital after botched procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "When it does happen, it can be devastating for the patient," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He recalls seeing men with "skin necrosis, where an area of the skin dies off it turns very black and then it sort of sloughs off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "So, men will go in thinking, 'Oh, it's gonna be brilliant', but they might come out actually being even more dissatisfied than when they went in." Alex, who did not want his real name to be used, travelled to Germany for a different type of penis enhancement procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He had surgery to cut the ligament that attaches the penis to the pubic bone to make it appear longer.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He also had his own fat cells harvested and injected into his penis to enlarge it.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: When he woke up after the procedure, he was in so much pain he couldn't stand.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I sustained a lot of bruising and all my upper legs turned yellow," Alex says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I couldn't walk properly for about a month." Alex was treated in Modgil's clinic where eventually he was given the all-clear.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "Many people do not get that luxury," he says.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "I got off lucky." Alex says he knows he was "never small in the first place", but society and porn had convinced him that a bigger penis was "masculine and the best".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: There is a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term Despite a lack of official data on the number of penile enhancement procedures, Modgil says online search trends, advertising and social media all "points to the fact that the numbers are on the up".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This has led the British Association of Urological Surgeons to issue new recommendations against these procedures.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: "The guidance that we've recently produced essentially says we cannot recommend that any of these procedures should take place because the evidence is so poor," says Modgil.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: It looked at 36 studies, involving 3,750 men, but said it was still not clear what the "safety profile" of these procedures were.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: This is partly down to a lack of data on how fillers affect the penis long-term.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: But there is also concern that - just like lip fillers - you do not need any qualifications to perform the procedure.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Modgil says an outright ban is "probably too severe", but if these procedures are going to continue then the industry "massively needs regulation".
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: He called for a national registry to record when penis filler procedures have been performed and for long-term data to be collected so men can make an informed decision based on the risks and the benefits.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: Back in Manchester, Jason is happy with the results of his procedure and thinks he'll do it again when his current fillers wear off.
sentences.article_title: What's driving men to get penis fillers, despite the risks?

sentences.text: A million young people are being offered a free meningitis B vaccine.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It comes after concerns over the UK's largest and fastest growing outbreak that happened in Kent earlier this year.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Nearly 90,000 doses of the vaccine have already been given, with 135,000 more booked in for the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: So who needs the vaccine, what's in it and where can you get it for free?
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine offers protection against a dangerous strain of meningitis called meningitis B (MenB) that caused the outbreak in Kent.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: The vaccine does not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: It is common to get some swelling, redness or tenderness where you have the injection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You may also get a mild fever, nausea, headache or muscle aches but these symptoms should disappear after one or two days.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: More serious side effects are rare.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Bookings can be made at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Other students under the age of 25 who are heading to a residential college or university this autumn for the first time can also contact a participating pharmacy.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: You do not need to be registered with a GP surgery to use the walk-in service.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Find a participating pharmacy here , external .
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Both doses are needed for the fullest protection.
sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.article_title: Starting uni? What to know about the free NHS meningitis B jab in England

sentences.text: Vaccination can save lives.

sentences.text: As temperatures exceed 30C (86F) in some parts of the UK this week, the last thing people want to do is turn on the oven.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Not only can cooking in hot weather feel like a chore, but many of us find ourselves feeling less hungry altogether.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So when the heat gets too much, should we consider changing our diet?
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Here are three things to think about next time you're hot and hungry.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking chicken in an air fryer uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven "There's no need for more protein in a heatwave," says Aisling Daly, senior lecturer in nutrition at Oxford Brookes University.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But if you fancy it, some of the most common proteins will need cooking (like meat, chicken and fish) and that can be off-putting in the heat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even an outdoor BBQ can be too hot to handle.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Cooking a chicken leg in the worktop device uses less than half the energy of a conventional oven, according to Radio 4's Sliced Bread .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And because they are smaller and speedier, they also pump less heat into your kitchen.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But experts say don't forget about your slightly less fashionable slow cooker - likely buried in the back of your cupboard.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even though they run for longer, they're typically more energy efficient and release even less heat than the air fryer.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: The reality, though, is that simply by eating and digesting protein, our bodies produce more heat than other food groups.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That's due to the energy needed by the stomach, intestines and liver to break down and absorb these complex molecules.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So that steak you crave will only bring you out in a sweat.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But you can also get your protein from lentils, nuts, milk, tofu and cheese too.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: To reduce body heat while still getting your protein fix, Dr Daly recommends focusing on things like bean salads, eggs, pre-cooked meats and plenty of Greek yoghurt (frozen too).
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Making a smoothie by blending up fruit, veg and yogurt (while adding in peanut butter for protein) can provide a balanced, nutritious meal in an easy way.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: And it might also be time to turn to some lighter fish, such as tuna, salmon or prawns.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: When it's hot, we lose water when we sweat, so we need to replace it or we become dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Six to eight glasses of fluid a day is normally recommended by the NHS, , external and in a heatwave you could need a lot more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "There is no single amount that suits everyone, because how much fluid your body needs depends on lots of factors like your age, body size, activity levels and health status," says Dr Charlotte Mills, food and nutrition scientist at the University of Reading.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: World Cup footballers aren't the only ones who benefit from hydration breaks: other athletes and pregnant and breastfeeding women are among those who need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: But rehydrating doesn't just mean refilling your water bottle every couple of hours.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: "We need to eat our water as well as drink it," says Dr Daly, "80-90% of fruit and vegetables are full of water." Cucumber, tomatoes, lettuce, celery, watermelon and strawberries all have very high water content, above 90%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Apples, carrots, cooked broccoli and pears contain 80% to 89% water, as do oranges, grapes and pineapple.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: In comparison, boiled eggs are 75% water , external , with digestive biscuits only 2.8% water , external .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Even a cheese and tomato pizza is 38% water, with takeaway chips containing as much as 51%.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If your mouth has dried up just reading this, try some of these water-rich recipes .
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: A useful way to check if you're hydrated is to check the colour of your urine.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Pale yellow is what you're after.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: If it's orangey or dark brown, that's a sign that your kidneys - which filter waste products and produce urine - are holding onto water because there isn't enough in the body.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: That means you're dehydrated and need to drink more.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down We know some people love a cuppa, even when it's sweltering, and that actually makes scientific sense.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Warm or room-temperature drinks are just as good as cold ones for cooling you down, says Dr Daly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Research suggests your body sweats more quickly to get rid of the excess heat after a hot drink.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: After a cold drink, your body sweats more slowly.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Your body is trying to keep your core temperature steady at about 37 degrees celsius.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: So hot tea won't necessarily help you cool down more quickly - the key thing is to stay hydrated no matter the temperature of the liquid.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You don't need to shun your favourite coffee either just because it's hot - although too much caffeine can make the body produce more urine, and leave you dehydrated.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: For matcha fans, the drink contains more caffeine than a cup of tea but less than a regular coffee.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Dr Daly says one or two coffees a day should make little difference to your hydration levels - but five or six will start to have an effect.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Bear in mind that drinking alcohol also dehydrates.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: You could structure your day differently too, and take a southern European approach to eating.
sentences.article_title: More protein or less? The foods to get you through a heatwave

sentences.text: Have an early breakfast, an afternoon siesta while it's very hot and then a late dinner.

sentences.text: As a period of extreme heat is forecast across the UK this week, UV levels are expected to be high in many areas.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Some exposure to UV is essential for our wellbeing, but too much is damaging and can cause skin cancer.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: UV radiation is emitted by the Sun and penetrates the Earth's atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It enables our skin to produce essential vitamin D, which is important for the function of bones, blood cells and our immune system.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: But too much UV can be harmful.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It can lead to skin cancer by damaging DNA in skin cells.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: UV also plays a substantial role in skin ageing, contributing to wrinkles and loosened folds.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It has also been linked to eye problems , external , including cataracts.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "Every exposure to UV, especially every sunburn, increases our risk of skin cancer," says Prof Dorothy Bennett, from St George's, University of London.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "Melanoma, the most dangerous skin cancer, is now the fifth commonest cancer in the UK." UK's hottest May day record broken for second day in a row How long will the heatwave last?
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Why temperature records are being not only broken but smashed Levels of UV radiation vary throughout the day.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: The highest readings are in the four-hour period around "solar noon", when the sun is at its highest - usually from late morning to early afternoon.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: The UV Index (or UVI) is a measure of ultraviolet radiation used around the world.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Values start at zero and can rise above 10.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: The higher the number, the greater the potential for damage to the skin and eyes, and the less time it takes for harm to occur.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: In the UK, the UV index would typically be around 5-6 during the summer, with a maximum of 8 only in exceptional circumstances.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Countries close to the equator can experience very high UV levels in the middle of the day, throughout the year.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Nairobi in Kenya, for example, can have UV levels above 10 all year, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Majorca in Spain normally hits nine in June and July.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Appropriate sunscreen is essential.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Some sun protection is required when UK levels are medium (3-5) or high (6-7), the WHO says.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Extra sun protection is required when UV levels are very high (8-10) or extremely high (11+).
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: Children are more sensitive to UV radiation than adults, and therefore require additional protection at lower levels than adults.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: The NHS advises , external using sunscreen with an SPF factor of 30 or above and which offers at least 4-star UVA protection.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It should be applied to all exposed skin, including the face, neck and ears - and head if you have thinning or no hair - ideally 30 minutes before you go out into the sun.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: As a guide, adults should aim to apply about six to eight teaspoons of sunscreen if covering the entire body.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: It should be reapplied every two hours, or sooner if you sweat a lot, have been in water, or after drying yourself with a towel.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: In addition, the NHS recommends: covering up with suitable clothing and wearing sunglasses spending time in the shade when the sun is strongest - between 11:00 and 15:00 from March to October in the UK What should you look for when choosing sunscreen?
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: There is no safe or healthy way to get a tan, according to the NHS. , external Dr Bav Shergill from the British Association of Dermatologists recommends using self-tan products instead.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "When you tan, ultraviolet light stimulates your skin cells to produce pigment to try and protect the DNA of skin cells - but that protection is minimal -  the equivalent of SP4.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "That is not much protection at all - so you can still burn very early," he warns.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: The amount of UV reaching your skin is not driven by the daily temperature.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "Your skin can burn just as quickly whether it's 30C or 20C," warns BBC Weather's BBC Weather's Helen Willetts.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "Don't be caught out on cloudy days.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: UV will still penetrate thin clouds - so even if you don't think it's that sunny, you can still burn." Yes, according to Dr Shergill.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "The skin may look darker, but it doesn’t always behave that way from a protection point of view  – because there are more genes at play than we think about," he says.
sentences.article_title: What are UV levels and how can you protect yourself?

sentences.text: "I have, for example, seen South Asian people with skin cancer and I have seen people with dual-heritage get skin cancer." The broader risks of eye damage and harmful effects on the immune system from too much UV radiation affect people of all skin colour.

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston trains for her powerlifting competitions at a gym in Redditch A teenage powerlifter managed to win double golds at a world championship despite her endometriosis flaring up to leave her in excruciating pain just before the competition.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: Lhamo Weston, from Redditch, also landed second on the podium with a silver and a bronze medal, across three events in the World Sub-Junior & Junior Powerlifting Championships, in South Africa last month.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: The 18-year-old only took up the sport three years ago, after being inspired by her brother to give it a go.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

She stood on the podium in the Under 57kg category at the championship after getting two golds in squat and deadlift, and a bronze in the bench event.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "It felt incredible to be completely honest, I went into it with expectations of potentially reaching podium.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "There's not enough awareness about it and how it actually impacts women and girls," she continued.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: "I've been dealing with endometriosis since I was 12, and I only got diagnosed last year.
sentences.article_title: Powerlifter wins golds despite endometriosis pain

sentences.text: It was a very long journey and I just think there needs to be more awareness so we can try and find solutions to help other people.

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd was diagnosed with breast cancer in 2019 A breast cancer survivor says she no longer lives "with the same fear" after a clinical trial enabled her to stop the heart medication she needed following cancer treatment.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: Lucy Shepherd, from Hertfordshire, was diagnosed with triple positive breast cancer shortly after her 33rd birthday, but a routine scan revealed that her heart function had declined during care.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: A new study, described as "hugely encouraging" for patients, has found the majority of breast cancer survivors whose treatment caused heart problems may not need to be on precautionary medication for life.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'

sentences.text: "Being part of the trial and having the chance to come off my heart medication has definitely improved my life," Shepherd said.
sentences.article_title: Heart trial after breast cancer has 'improved my life'
