sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Share your challenges, tips and questions with us ahead of the return to school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Friends Amelia (left) and Beatrice (right) are living at home when they start university this September More new students are choosing to live at home for university this year than in the last nine years, new data shows.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Over 81,000 UK 18-year-olds said in their accepted university application that they intended to live at home this year, according to the Universities and Colleges Admissions Service (Ucas) - just over one in three students in that category.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: In 2017, it was closer to one in five.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: The figures vary across the UK - with 48% of applicants in Scotland intending to live at home, compared with 20% in Wales - but the trend is rising across the board.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Students told the BBC the rising cost of living was a major influence in deciding what to do after school or college.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: For friends Beatrice and Amelia, who are from St Helens, Merseyside, the cost of accommodation was a big factor in their decision to live at home while studying.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Both are heading to university in September, but neither will be moving into student accommodation.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Beatrice is going to the University of Manchester to study maths and plans to commute by train, a journey which can take about 50 minutes in total.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "My first choice was Manchester and then my second was Liverpool, so I knew I could commute," she says, adding that the price of accommodation would have been "a few grand a year".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Amelia, who is going to study at Liverpool John Moores University - approximately 20 minutes away by train - says the accommodation she found was between £300 and £400 a week.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: Although neither is looking forward to the commute, both are still hoping they can get the full experience of university while living at home.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: My three-hour university commute is worth the £7,000 saving on halls However, fellow student Jessica, who is also going to study at Liverpool John Moores University, feels she will miss out.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: She says she would have loved to live on campus and enjoy student life, but the price of renting is "ridiculous" and "insane".
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "I have a part-time job as everything is so expensive, and then commuting is going to kill a lot of my free time as well," she says.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.text: "It is a bit sad really when you think about it." But she is pleased that staying at home means she will still be able to have her mum and dad's cooked dinners.
sentences.article_title: More students planning to live at home for university over 'insane' living costs

sentences.article_title: Conservationist honoured for protecting rare animals

The Isle of Man's Space Registry handles satellite filings for some major space operators.

sentences.article_title: Manx space group urges election candidates to back treaty

sentences.text: Anthropic says it has identified and disrupted attempts to use its AI model for "malicious activity" which could support the development of biological weapons.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The findings, made in the firm's recent threat intelligence report, is the latest in a growing series of warnings from AI researchers and industry insiders about the technology's potential risks to humanity .
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The warnings have prompted calls to action, with US Senator Bernie Sanders demanding a pause on advanced AI development and a ban on artificial superintelligence.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: President Donald Trump has so far rejected such fears, saying on Thursday he was concerned "if we don't win AI, we're going to be put in a very bad position".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The company published its latest threat intelligence report , external on Thursday.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Such reports have become a regular feature across the AI industry as firms seek to demonstrate how they identify and disrupt attempts to misuse their models.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: This includes Google, which wrote on Tuesday , external that a person had attempted to use its AI tool, Gemini, to obtain a "complete, step-by-step technical guide for synthesizing weaponised biological agents".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Claude, Anthropic's AI model was also used by actors linked to a Russia-based cyber espionage campaign and by an Iranian propaganda institution, according to its report.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The cases of concern detected over the past eight months ranged from fake dating apps and hotel Wifi scams, to surveillance built to identify dissidents.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Anthropic has also accused Chinese AI firms of trying to replicate Claude's capabilities.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The lengthy report lists cases in which suspected state-sponsored groups, criminals, spyware vendors, state propaganda institutions and politically motivated individuals misused its technology.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "Malicious use" of its Claude Haiku, Sonnet, and Opus models was disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026, it said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: None of the misuse cases involved Claude Fable or the powerful Mythos-class models, with the exception of one instance of distillation - the process for training smaller AI models using larger, more expensive models.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: As well as detecting the use of its models for cyber and influence operations, surveillance, scams and fraud and weapon development, Anthropic said it had blocked scientists who used its AI in ways that could support biological weapons development.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The report highlighted "five case studies of actors using our models in ways that could support biological weapons development".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Biological misuse, it said, is "one of the most serious risks of frontier AI model".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Without the correct safeguards, such capabilities "could have catastrophic consequences", Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "The same information that can be used to develop a biological weapon could also be used to develop, for example, a vaccine or a cure for a disease," Anthropic said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Jacob Klein, the head of threat intelligence at Anthropic, told the New York Times , external it was "an incredibly nuanced situation".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "You are not seeing someone in a comic book kind of way say, 'Hey, I want to build a biological weapon to kill everybody,'" he said.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The report also noted six cases where Claude was used "to develop software for conventional weapons, including firearms, missiles, armed drones, bombs, and other munitions, as well as the targeting and control systems that operate them".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Why some experts increasingly fear AI will take over Anthropic researcher believes more than 10% chance AI 'could kill all humans' The report indicated that cybercriminals and state-backed hackers have increasingly used its technology to assist their operations.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Hacking group ShinyHunters, as well as China-based labs, were among those named in the report.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The report also said that a hacking group whose work is consistent with the Russia-based Midnight Blizzard allegedly used AI to build a system that automatically detected when its malware was flagged by security defences and rewrote code until it evaded detection.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The California-based company said it had incorporated its findings into its processes "to better prevent, detect, and disrupt these activities in the future".
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: Anthropic said it had shared intelligence with authorities and industry partners where appropriate.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: In an article published on 6 September, OpenAI chief scientist Jakub Pachocki called for the industry to implement "voluntary slowdowns" until safeguards are set.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "I am concerned no one is prepared for the consequences of a continued rapid rise in machine intelligence," Pachocki said, adding that OpenAI, which makes ChatGPT, will continue its work on building safeguards, though broader interventions are required.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: The warning prompted an open letter to UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham calling for a new multinational treaty for the safe development of AI and a call for governments to collaborate about what a treaty based on the development of superintelligence should look like.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: In the US, Democratic lawmaker Bernie Sanders has introduced legislation to ban AI  superintelligence and temporarily pause advanced AI development.
sentences.article_title: Anthropic blocks possible attempt to use AI to make biological weapons

sentences.text: "When scientists tell you there is a chance, a chance that it could have a cataclysmic impact on humanity, you've got be a moron not to say, slow it down," he said on Thursday on BBC's Newsnight .

sentences.text: On Tuesday, Sony will release Marvel's Wolverine - the biggest game exclusive to the PlayStation 5 this year.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It's made by Insomniac, the studio responsible for the recent Spider-Man titles, which have sold 50 million copies in recent years.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: But unlike the friendly neighbourhood superhero, Wolverine has a Pegi-18 rating in the UK, meaning a child cannot legally buy the game, and it contains considerable levels of blood, gore and violence.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It represents a gamble for the studio responsible for some of Sony's biggest hits - will it turn out to have been worth it?
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: This review does not reveal the game's biggest moments, but beware minor spoilers for some of the characters that appear and a few early sequences.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Some of the images contain blood.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: The BBC’s Tom Gerken gets his claws on Marvel's Wolverine You play as Logan, aka Wolverine, the comic book superhero that can self-heal and has retractable claws.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Donning the famous yellow-and-black outfit (among others), you hack and slash your way through hordes of enemies.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The combat is free-flowing and easy to pick up, as Wolverine stabs and slices his foes with copious amounts of blood on display.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Still, some may feel it doesn't go far enough.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Combat is built around a "rage" meter which fills as you take down enemies, with a full meter turning your surroundings grey and allowing you to swiftly dispatch your foes There are some stealth options, but I generally ignored them and went in with my claws out.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The game didn't penalise me for this.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: You also unlock a slew of abilities, much like other games in the genre, meaning you get even more powerful as the game rumbles on.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And a clever system allows you to spend the rage you have accumulated to regenerate your health.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: The combat kept me hooked the whole way through the game, which took about 20 hours to get to the end credits.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: My colleague was faster, clocking in at about 15 hours.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It was so influential that it spawned a popular online gag, pointing fun at reviewers who couldn't help but repeat a cliché , external about the game making them feel like Spider-Man.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "There's a significant shake-up happening here in game design terms," freelance game critic Emma Kent told me.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Insomniac is moving away from Spider-Man's open world formula to adopt a linear structure for Wolverine.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "That means less open exploration, and a more curated path through the game world." The combat is broken up by short sequences where you explore high-detailed environments, which while fun at first began to drag as the game went on It adds to the gamble that comes with the game having such graphic violence.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Peter Parker and Miles Morales would go out of their way to avoid killing enemies - stringing them up or gluing them against walls with his webs - and there was no real gore to speak of," Kent said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Some games truly revel in showing detailed and over-exaggerated gore, but the violence in Marvel's Wolverine doesn't feel particularly gratuitous.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And the game's director Mike Daly accepted this came with a risk.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Even though this character appeals to kids, making a game that is explicitly like, 'sorry, this is not for kids, you should not play this game' - it does reduce the scope," he said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "But I think there was no other way to do it.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: That was the cost of doing business if we really wanted to set a game with this character in this universe." The graphics are great, but small cutscenes like this broke up the action too frequently for my taste One thing I didn't expect was the game's reliance on its performers.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Gameplay is frequently interrupted with cutscenes, which will I'm sure prove divisive.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Nonetheless, the acting is top drawer, with the standout being veteran performer Troy Baker (known for many roles including Joel in The Last of Us) who puts in a memorable performance as Nathaniel Essex.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Liam McIntyre, who plays Wolverine, told BBC Newsbeat he was "looking forward to people playing it".
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "I'm so proud that people are resonating with the story, with the performances, the character," he said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "This is such an astoundingly good character piece.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "I'm so happy that I've been able to make a Wolverine that hopefully people love." And to that point - when Hugh Jackman's famous take on the character last appeared on the big screen in 2024's Deadpool & Wolverine, it made $205m (then £160m) on opening weekend in the US - the best ever opening for an R-rated film.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It all suggests Sony's gamble may be a safer bet than it first seems.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Deadpool & Wolverine ultimately grossed $1.3bn worldwide at the box office,  suggesting there was a much bigger audience than expected for 18-rated violence The way you leap from building to building is superb, and feels excellent to control.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: But I'd rather there had been fewer acting sequences and more gameplay.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: On one or two occasions, in a cutscene Wolverine did something which felt like it broke a cardinal rule of game design to me - never show the player something cool when you could have let them do it themselves.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Still - the performances are of a high quality.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "Troy and Liam in particular are performers where they get really invested in their characters and subject matter," Daly said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "They are part of the problem solving squad for who they are and how they bring that out - they brought a lot to the table.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: Clearly the developers were inspired by narrative adventures like Uncharted for this kind of storytelling, and the gameplay even feels similar at times with chase and climbing sequences.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And while that game was genre-defining, it came out almost 20 years ago, so it's hardly a favourable comparison.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: In fact, perhaps the biggest issue for Wolverine is that it doesn't reinvent the wheel like Spider-Man did.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: It's a game packed with tight combat and excellent performances, but it never threatens to meet the genre-defining heights of Insomniac's previous offering.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: And Daly said there was a "monumental" amount of pressure that came with making the game following the success of Spider-Man - but as to whether the gamble paid off, he took a Zen view.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "I measure success when I hear people talk to me about the game, who are Wolverine fans, and they say 'thank you for making this, you nailed it'," he said.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: "If I hear that, it's like, yes, we did it.
sentences.article_title: PlayStation gambles with 18-rated Wolverine game - will it pay off?

sentences.text: That's what we set out to do." I survived two years as prime minister in a hit new game - then my cabinet deserted me Is the Assassin's Creed Black Flag remake worth the 13 year wait?

sentences.text: Google will buy up to half the electricity produced by one of Finland's nuclear power plants as part of a record €13bn (£11bn; $15bn) investment in the country's AI infrastructure, the company announced.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: The US tech giant said the package would fund three new data centres, expand an existing site and support energy projects to power growing demand for AI services.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "This is Google's largest single investment in Europe and a testament to Finland's leadership in responsibly building AI infrastructure," the company said on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "Google's decision is a clear testament to our strengths," Finland's Prime Minister Petteri Orpo said in a statement.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: As part of the deal, Google signed a 22-year contract with Finnish utility Fortum to buy up to 50% of the output from the Loviisa nuclear power plant.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Earlier this week, TikTok announced a $1bn investment in Finland to build a new data centre in Kouvola, pointing to the country's "strong digital infrastructure, clean energy mix, robust data governance and skilled tech talent".
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Finland has emerged as an attractive location for data centres because of its cool climate, plentiful low-carbon electricity and relatively uncongested power grid.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: The colder temperatures can reduce the energy needed to cool facilities packed with computer servers.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Technology companies are racing to secure power supplies as the AI boom drives demand for vast networks of data centres.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: The Google investment is expected to support more than 37,000 jobs during construction and boost Finland's GDP by €3.6bn a year, according to Google.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Construction is set to take place in 2027 and 2028.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "The value of the data economy extends far beyond direct investment into spurring innovation, research and development," Orpo added.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "Deepening our collaboration with Google will deliver lasting benefits for both parties." Google will build new data centres in Kajaani, Muhos and Vaala, while expanding its existing facility in Hamina, which it established after converting a former paper mill in 2009.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: The infrastructure will help support products such as its AI chatbot Gemini, alongside services including Search, Maps and YouTube.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Google said the investments also covered "clean energy projects, and dedicated nature and community funds to support local biodiversity, education, research, and workforce development".
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "Google is proud to deepen our roots in Finland," said Ruth Porat, president and chief investment officer of Alphabet and Google.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: "This investment underscores Google's commitment to grow our presence responsibly, pairing the expansion of our technical infrastructure with new energy capacity, grid enhancements, and energy affordability initiatives," she added.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: Earlier this year, Google's parent company Alphabet raised its global spending plans to as much as $205bn as it sought to expand computing capacity for AI services.
sentences.article_title: Google picks Finland for its largest single investment in Europe

sentences.text: David Etor's first break came after designing and building a kind of "solar oven" in Nigeria A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: David Etor, 43, who grew up in Nigeria, only learned to read and write aged 12 and was told as a child that "nothing good will come out of you", but is now a lecturer in the School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It worked incredibly well," he said, which led to an award from the state government and a job.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: That subsequently led him to receive a scholarship to study electrical power at Newcastle University and a PhD at Durham University, before he secured his current job in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Sir Steve Webb, the former MP and Pensions Minister, who got to know Etor through the church in Bristol, called his achievements "remarkable".

sentences.text: "They shouldn't be written off." "I was pinching myself on my way here this morning," Etor added.

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong
